newsitem.title: USA: Republicans censor documents in funds probe.
newsitem.headline: Republicans censor documents in funds probe.

text.p: By Alan Elsner, U.S. Political Correspondent
The Republican National Committee has heavily censored documents sent to Senate investigators probing possible campaign fund-raising misdeeds, a Democratic source said on Thursday.
The RNC sent about 10,000 pages of documents in response to subpoenas issued by the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee, which is investigating alleged illegalities in the 1996 elections.

The committee was investigating whether China and other foreign interests sought to influence U.S. foreign policy by helping President Bill Clinton and the Democratic Party with illegal political contributions.
It also was looking at possible Republican financial links to foreign business interests. The FBI and a House committee were conducting simultaneous but separate investigations.
The source said one of every four pages were heavily censored with the names of people, organisations and internal comments blacked out.
"They have no legal right to do this. No other entity has done anything like this -- not the White House or the Democratic National Committee," said the source.
The White House has blacked out parts of documents that refer to other issues. The DNC has blacked out private information such as individuals' social security numbers.
The RNC has said it reserved the right to black out parts of the documents it does not consider relevant to the investigation.

The source said the ranking Democrat on the committee, Ohio Sen. John Glenn, viewed the Republican action as an insult and would ask committee chairman, Tennessee Republican Sen. Fred Thompson, to take action.
Thompson hopes to begin public hearings in early July, perhaps starting the week of July 8, although no firm date has been set.
The latest development was a new blow to the spirit of bipartisanship in the investigation. Last week, Democrats on the committee said Thompson was rejecting many of their demands to issue subpoenas.

Democrats want to investigate a think tank established by the Republicans which received a $2 million loan guarantee from a Hong Kong company. The Republicans returned $122,000 to the company earlier this month when it learned the money came from overseas.
The Democratic Party, which is deeply in debt, has returned $1.5 million which it suspected came from foreign interests and promised to repay another $1.5 million as soon as it can afford to do so.
Much of that money came from Asian business interests or individuals who have since fled the country or who have refused to cooperate with the investigation.
